milestones: it is fast enough to be interesting
IO cost is measured, not asserted
a mesh is a sparse matrix to me
the room survives its own memory budget
the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
real photos flow through a real pipeline
the world and the first city are mine

tickets.title: Derive the 3DGS projection Jacobian and check against finite differences
tickets.done_when: J written out by hand and matching a numerical finite-difference check

tickets.title: Bake lighting and materials on the Old Trafford GLB
tickets.done_when: old-trafford.glb re-exported with baked lighting/materials, dropped into public/models/, and it visibly reads as lit (not flat) in the running site

tickets.title: Swap the baked model into the live site
tickets.done_when: deployed site loads the newly baked old-trafford.glb and the stadium looks lit, not the current weak/placeholder version

tickets.title: Decide which stands/angles to present and in what order
tickets.done_when: a short ordered list exists (in story.js or a note) naming each camera-preset stop and the one idea each stop should land

tickets.title: Write the on-page text for each stand stop
tickets.done_when: every stop in story.js has finished copy — no placeholder text left anywhere in the scroll-story

tickets.title: Scaffold the site with a static placeholder letter on scroll
tickets.done_when: a new repo/site loads and scrolling reveals a static (non-animated) placeholder letter — proves the project shell and scroll wiring work before any animation is built

tickets.title: Animate the letter unfolding as you scroll
tickets.done_when: scrolling through the intro shows the letter physically unfolding (not just fading in), tied to scroll position, with placeholder text still fine at this stage

tickets.title: Write the "Dear Manchester United" letter
tickets.done_when: full letter text written, starting "Dear Manchester United," finished and dropped into the site in place of placeholder copy

tickets.title: Render a fixed 2D Gaussian to a bitmap, no camera
tickets.done_when: a bitmap image file shows a single 2D Gaussian blob rendered from a hardcoded mean/covariance, no camera or projection involved yet

tickets.title: Quaternion + scale to 3x3 covariance, checked against a known rotation
tickets.done_when: function converting (quaternion, scale) to a 3x3 covariance matrix, output verified against a hand-computed known rotation case

tickets.title: Project one 3D Gaussian to a screen-space ellipse and render it
tickets.done_when: a single 3D Gaussian, given a camera, projects to a screen-space ellipse and renders as a recognizable blob at the right screen position

tickets.title: Write and launch a vector-add CUDA kernel, verified against CPU output
tickets.done_when: a CUDA kernel adds two arrays on the GPU and its output matches a CPU-computed reference exactly, on real hardware (not just compiled)

tickets.title: Work out a thread/block/grid indexing scheme by hand for a 2D problem
tickets.done_when: a 2D kernel (e.g. matrix element-wise op) correctly indexes every element exactly once, with the block/grid math written out by hand and matching the running result

tickets.title: Derive the ALE weak form of Navier-Stokes
tickets.done_when: the ALE-reformulated weak form is written out by hand in full, with the mesh-velocity convective term explicit, and checked against the standard Eulerian weak form in the limiting case of zero mesh velocity

tickets.title: Write up the ALE weak-form derivation cleanly
tickets.done_when: the LaTeX draft ships with correct boundary-contribution signs on all eight walls, the KBC in level-set form in both dimensional and nondimensional sections, hats consistent on convective terms, the free-surface residual integrand wrapped in brackets, DOF counts fixed on the ansatz ($n_v$ for velocity/mesh, $n_p$ for pressure), and no `\bm{n^1}` brace bugs or `\bm{n}^1\bm{n}^1` juxtapositions remaining

tickets.title: Scaffold the FlashAttention repo with kernels/ and notebooks/
tickets.done_when: a repo exists with kernels/ and notebooks/, a notebook successfully imports a function from kernels/, and a naive attention reference implementation lives in kernels/ for later tests to compare against

tickets.title: Derive the online softmax rescale factor by hand
tickets.done_when: the rescale factor exp(m_old - m_new) is written out with the step showing why a running normalizer computed under an old max must be corrected when the max updates, not asserted from the paper

tickets.title: Implement tiled forward attention with a running output accumulator
tickets.done_when: an outer loop over Q blocks and inner loop over K/V blocks maintaining m, l, and a rescaled running output accumulator passes torch.allclose against the naive attention reference, for at least two block sizes that do not evenly divide the sequence length

tickets.title: Derive the backward identity dS = P * (dP - D)
tickets.done_when: dS = P * (dP - D) with D_i = rowsum(dO * O)_i is derived in full from the softmax Jacobian, including the step showing sum_k P_ik dP_ik = sum_k O_ik dO_ik, and checked numerically against a finite-difference dS on a small input

tickets.title: Instrument the loops to count HBM reads and writes by block size
tickets.milestone: IO cost is measured, not asserted
tickets.done_when: the forward and backward loops report counted HBM reads and writes as a function of block size, with the count derived from the loop structure and cross-checked by hand for one small configuration

tickets.title: Implement blockwise online softmax and test against one-pass softmax
tickets.done_when: a blockwise softmax maintaining running max m and running normalizer l matches a one-pass softmax to float64 tolerance on random inputs, including an input with a large positive outlier that would overflow a naive exp

tickets.title: Save per-row logsumexp from the forward pass
tickets.done_when: the tiled forward returns per-row logsumexp alongside the output, matching torch.logsumexp on the naive attention scores to float64 tolerance

tickets.title: Implement the tiled backward pass with recomputation, verified by gradcheck
tickets.done_when: torch.autograd.gradcheck passes on a small float64 input, S and P are recomputed inside the loop from Q, K, V and the saved logsumexp, and a peak-memory check confirms no N x N buffer is ever allocated

tickets.title: Plot measured HBM traffic against the O(N^2 d^2 / M) bound
tickets.milestone: IO cost is measured, not asserted
tickets.done_when: measured HBM traffic is plotted against the O(N^2 d^2 / M) bound across block sizes, with any departure from the bound's shape explained rather than noted

tickets.title: Build the mesh incidence matrices from a loaded triangle mesh
tickets.milestone: a mesh is a sparse matrix to me
tickets.done_when: vertex-edge and edge-face incidence matrices are built as scipy sparse matrices for a loaded mesh, and d1 @ d0 is verified to be the zero matrix, which is the discrete statement that the boundary of a boundary is empty

tickets.title: Derive the cotangent weights from the Dirichlet energy
tickets.milestone: a mesh is a sparse matrix to me
tickets.done_when: the cotan weight (cot alpha + cot beta)/2 is derived by taking the gradient of a piecewise-linear hat function over a triangle and integrating the Dirichlet energy, with the step showing where the cotangents come from geometrically, not quoted from the paper

tickets.title: Assemble the cotan Laplacian and mass matrix, verified against libigl
tickets.milestone: a mesh is a sparse matrix to me
tickets.done_when: hand-assembled L and M match igl.cotmatrix and igl.massmatrix to numerical tolerance, L is verified symmetric with rows summing to zero, and L applied to a constant function returns zero on interior vertices

tickets.title: Find where the cotan Laplacian breaks on obtuse and degenerate triangles
tickets.milestone: a mesh is a sparse matrix to me
tickets.done_when: a mesh with obtuse triangles is shown to produce negative cotan weights, the consequence for the maximum principle is stated concretely, and the difference between barycentric and Voronoi mass matrices on that mesh is measured rather than described

tickets.title: Derive the quadric error metric and the optimal contraction point
tickets.done_when: the 4x4 quadric Q is derived as the sum of outer products of plane equations so that v^T Q v is the sum of squared distances to those planes, and the 3x3 system for the optimal contraction position is obtained by setting the gradient to zero, including what to do when that system is singular

tickets.title: Implement QEM edge-collapse decimation with a priority queue
tickets.done_when: a mesh decimates to a target triangle count with quadrics accumulated on collapse and the queue updated lazily, and the result is a valid manifold with no degenerate or flipped triangles, checked rather than eyeballed

tickets.title: Compare QEM output against Blender's Decimate modifier
tickets.done_when: the same mesh is decimated to the same ratio by both implementations and compared by Hausdorff distance to the original, with any systematic difference traced to a specific choice (boundary handling, collapse validity, or the singular-quadric fallback) rather than left as noise

tickets.title: Write the United history timeline content as structured data
tickets.done_when: a JSON or JS module holds every timeline entry with date, title, and a written blurb, covering the eras a newcomer needs (Busby Babes, Munich, 68 European Cup, Ferguson, 99 treble, post-Ferguson), with no placeholder text in any entry

tickets.title: Build the scrollable timeline component from the entry data
tickets.done_when: the timeline renders every entry from NZ-41 in chronological order, is navigable by scroll on both desktop and a phone viewport, and adding a new entry to the data file makes it appear with no component change

tickets.title: Test the timeline on someone who knows nothing about United
tickets.done_when: someone with no United knowledge scrolls the timeline unaided and can afterwards say who Busby was, what happened at Munich, and why 1999 mattered, with any question they had to ask out loud turned into an edit of the entry that failed them

tickets.title: Pick the songs and write the lyric annotations by hand
tickets.done_when: a data file lists each song with its Spotify track ID, the specific lyric lines quoted, and a written note on what those lines have to do with United, for every song on the page with none left unannotated

tickets.title: Build the music page with Spotify embeds and reveal-on-click annotations
tickets.done_when: every song from NZ-44 renders as a Spotify embed, clicking one reveals its lyric lines and note, and the page is verified to still render the annotations when embeds are blocked by a tracker blocker or offline

tickets.title: Evaluate a free football API for squad stats and fixtures
tickets.done_when: one API is chosen with a working key, and a written note records its free-tier request limit, how far behind live its score updates actually run, whether per-player season stats are on the free tier at all, and whether its terms allow displaying the data on a public site

tickets.title: Build the squad stats page against the chosen API
tickets.done_when: the current squad renders with per-player stats from the NZ-46 API, responses are cached so a page refresh does not spend a fresh request, and the page shows a readable fallback rather than a blank grid when the API errors or the rate limit is hit

tickets.title: Add the live match layer for fixtures and in-progress scores
tickets.done_when: the next fixture shows when no match is on and the current score shows during one, polling only while a match is actually in progress, with the real update lag measured against a live match and stated on the page rather than implied to be real time

tickets.title: Link the United site and Old Trafford to each other
tickets.done_when: each deployed site carries a visible link to the other, both links are followed on a phone and a laptop without hitting a dead URL, and the two sites read as related rather than as two unrelated projects that happen to share a subject

tickets.title: Mount a second canvas and renderer inside the Traveling modal
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: opening the Traveling modal shows a spinning cube rendering inside the modal frame, the room's draw calls drop to zero while it is open and resume when it closes, and closing then reopening the modal five times does not increase the WebGL context count or blank the room canvas

tickets.title: Write disposeObject3D and prove it frees everything it allocated
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: adding and disposing a textured multi-material mesh 200 times leaves renderer.info.memory.geometries and .textures back within two of their starting values rather than climbing, and the utility handles meshes whose material is an array without throwing

tickets.title: Write places.js with New York, London and Manchester
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: a plain ES module exports countries and cities with slug-keyed lookups, at least one city omits the model key entirely and one includes it, photo paths are derived from the slug rather than stored, and importing it in the browser console returns the expected objects

tickets.title: Build the world and city views from code-generated placeholder boxes
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: clicking a box named CTRY-usa opens a disc of boxes named BLD-*, the back control returns to the world view, and the name matching runs through the same sanitizing helper the stadium uses so that a name containing a dot or a trailing underscore-digit still resolves

tickets.title: Render the photo filmstrip and highlight the building a photo belongs to
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: a city's photos render as lazy-loaded img elements beside the 3D view, hovering one turns its matching BLD- box the accent colour and unhovering restores the original material, a photo whose building is null highlights nothing without erroring, and no material is constructed during hover

tickets.title: Hold memory flat across repeated city swaps
tickets.milestone: the gallery engine works on placeholder boxes
tickets.done_when: clicking through every city twenty times and returning to the world view leaves renderer.info.memory.textures within two of its post-world value rather than climbing, and clicking two cities in quick succession on a throttled connection leaves exactly one disc in the scene

tickets.title: Add missing content to the ALE writeup
tickets.done_when: the LaTeX draft contains a notation table at the start of §2, the boundary-restricted basis $\phi_i^k$ defined once and cited from each wall paragraph, an LBB one-liner on why pressure basis is one degree lower than velocity, the KBC residual compressed to a single-integral form, the free-surface endpoint term written explicitly as $[\phi_i t_x^1/\text{Ca}]_{s_a}^{s_b}$, $\mathbf{m}^1$ defined for the 1D case, the pinning BC $\eta(0,t) = \eta(L,t) = 0$, the initial condition $\mathbf{u}(x,z,0) = 0$ and $\eta(x,0) = \eta_0(x)$, and one sentence stating that $\lambda^k, \gamma^k$ close via Lagrange multipliers on the no-slip constraint

tickets.title: Draft the Discretization section of the ALE writeup
tickets.done_when: §4 (Discretization) contains the master-element setup with the Jacobian change of variables $\int_K f\,dA = \int_{\hat K} f|J|\,d\hat A$ written out, the implicit-Euler time step on the ALE-hat coefficients ($\dot{\hat u}_j \to (\hat u_j^{k+1} - \hat u_j^k)/\delta t$), a stated block structure for the per-step nonlinear system (velocity / pressure / mesh / boundary-stress blocks), one line saying Newton iteration handles the convective nonlinearity, and pseudocode-style assembly loop over triangles with local matrix scatter into a global sparse matrix

tickets.title: Read the axisymmetric reference writeup and note the delta
tickets.done_when: a one-page note in the vault lists every place the axisymmetric reference formulation diverges from the 2D pool formulation (coordinate system, geometry-specific terms, boundary conditions that don't map, mesh handling), and flags which of those deltas affect the code that'll need to run for the reproduction milestone

tickets.title: Adopt the reference section-3 construction of the ALE-hat basis
tickets.done_when: §3 (Approximation) of the writeup defines $\hat\phi_j(\hat{\mathbf{x}})$ on the reference coords first and derives $\phi_j(x,z,t) = \hat\phi_j(\chi^{-1}(x,z,t))$ from it (matching the reference note's order, not the advisor's write-up which does it backwards), and states in one sentence why this ordering makes $\partial_t$ act only on the coefficients
